questions.ask: What is your year of birth?
What is the five-character customer code from your welcome letter?
What is your full date of birth?

intents.dispute: "This is not my debt" or "I never had this card".
intents.restructure: A request for a payment plan or lower repayments.
intents.vague: A vague period ("after payday") instead of an exact day.
intents.too_much: The customer says the full amount is too much.

lines.ask_today_multi: Could you pay the full amount today?

lines.date_past: That date has already passed. Which date from today onwards would work for you?
lines.not_business_day: That day is not a business day. Could you pay on {date} instead?
lines.after_deadline: The latest date I can record is {date}. Could you pay by then?
lines.vague_ask: Which exact day would that be?
lines.ask_date_for_amount: On which date could you pay {amount}?

assumptions: Business days are Monday to Saturday (workdays 0-5). Sunday and the holidays 2026-11-21, 2026-12-08 and 2026-12-25 are not business days.
The brief does not say how 'next <weekday>' is read. Default 'following_week' is used, in line with 'A week runs Monday to Sunday'.

Callback: today or either of the next two business days ('within_business_days:2'), business days only, later than now. Mon-Fri 09:00-18:00, Saturday 09:00-13:00 (both ends included), no callbacks on Sunday. The agent proposes one valid time and books nothing if it is refused (max_asks 2).
Identity: one wrong answer is forgiven over the whole check and the next one ends it, so max_wrong = 2 in total. The tool's own description says the same.

Identity answer formats: birth_year as 4 digits; customer_code as 5 capital letters/digits with no spaces; birth_date as %d.%m.%Y with leading zeros (03.04.1979). A date said only as numbers is read day-month-year.

verify_identity response fields: verified = 'correct', all_verified = 'identity_passed'. The API returns a running 'wrong_answers' count and a 'locked' flag but no 'wrong answers left' field or hint field, so 'left' and 'hint' are empty and the engine counts wrong answers against max_wrong. A badly formatted answer comes back ok=false and is not counted.
The brief does not say whether asking what the call is about counts as declining the questions. Default purpose_is_decline = true is used.
get_account returns one object 'account' (not an array). id_field = product_id, type_field = product_kind ('card' / 'overdraft').
All money is in euro cents: amount_scale = 100. create_promise also takes cents (amount_cents), so promise_scale = null. Example: 98 euros is sent as 9800.

Floor: card = statement_minimum_cents (floor_field). Overdraft has no floor field, so floor_pct 20 with floor_round 'up_unit' applies: 20% of amount_due_cents, rounded up to the next whole euro; an already whole euro is not raised (e.g. 48735 -> 9747 -> 9800; 50000 -> 10000). credit_limit_cents and overdraft_limit_cents are never used.

Not stated in the brief: if a floor exceeds the amount due (e.g. rounding up a tiny overdraft), the floor is capped at the full amount due. Accepted amounts run from the floor to the full amount due, both included.

Bands by days_overdue: early 1-15 (last business day of next week, 1 attempt); middle 16-40 (card: 8th business day after today, overdraft: 5th business day after today, 2 attempts); late 41-60 (the later of the last business day of the current month and the 3rd business day after today, 2 attempts).

Recoveries (61 or more days) is modelled as bands_outside -> event 'recoveries': no proposal and no promise, say a colleague now handles the account, transfer_to_agent queue 'recoveries', close handed_over/recoveries. A value of 0 or below should not occur and would be handled the same way.

Business-day counts start from tomorrow and never include today. Computed deadlines that are not business days move to the previous business day (e.g. Saturday 2026-11-21 is a holiday, so the end of that week becomes Friday 2026-11-20).

Rule 13: if the customer names a Sunday or holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the business day just before it. If that day is before today, offer the first business day after the named day.

Ladder: attempt 1 = the full amount (or the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much) on the 2nd business day after today. Attempt 2 (middle and late bands only) = the floor on the deadline. Refused offers are never repeated.

First ask is 'Could you pay the full amount today?' (first_ask 'today'). The floor offered after 'too much' (rule 17) is for the date just asked and uses no attempt, because only a flat refusal or a non-answer uses an attempt (too_much_floor 'asked_date').
A below-floor amount gets one floor offer; refusing it is a flat refusal. Refusing the deadline offered after a too-late date is also a flat refusal.
Hardship (rule 28): one sentence of sympathy, no persuasion, add_note 'vulnerable', then transfer to queue 'care' without asking for consent, then close handed_over/vulnerable.

Payment plan or lower repayments goes to queue payment_plans (handed_over/restructure). A request for a person: the agent asks once whether it can help, then transfers to customer_desk (handed_over/agent_request).
add_note is used only for system_fault (rule 24), paid_claim (26), disputed (27) and vulnerable (28). notes.enabled = false, and a refusal gets no note.

add_note has no product id field in the API (only customer_id, reason and optional free 'text'). The product id slot n_product is mapped to the optional 'text' field, so the note carries the product id as free text.
Brief says the call 'is recorded'. The opening says 'we record this call'.
The brief uses the call variables full_name and salutation instead of first_name, last_name and title, so they are declared in call_variables.
After a recorded promise, 'A confirmation letter will follow by post.' is the sms_line. Default ask_anything_else = true is kept.
The brief has no rule for changing a recorded promise, so the agent says it cannot be changed on this call.
The brief has no rule for what the verified customer should do if they ask for a callback, so callback_requested is not defined.
Single product per call: the multi settings are left at their defaults and have no effect.
